source.title: An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a positive real number alpha such that, for every integer n greater than or equal to 0, if alpha times (3/2)^n is written as g_n + r_n with g_n the greatest integer not greater than alpha times (3/2)^n and r_n its fractional part, then 0 <= r_n < 1/2? Equivalently, do any Z-numbers exist for the base 3/2 and the half-interval [0, 1/2)?

evidence.quote: We say that alpha is a Z-number if 0 <= r_n < 1/2 for all suffixes n >= 0.
Several years ago, a Japanese colleague proposed to me the problem whether such Z-numbers do in fact exist.

accepted.question_text: For sequences alpha times (3/2)^n with alpha a positive real number and n = 0, 1, 2, ..., can a theory analogous to the theory developed by Mahler for fractional parts lying in [0, 1/2) be established when the fractional parts are required to lie in subintervals of [0, 1) whose length is smaller than 1/2, possibly even arbitrarily small?

evidence.quote: It would be very interesting if a similar theory could be established for subintervals of smaller length, or perhaps even of arbitrarily small length.

accepted.question_text: For coprime integers p and q satisfying p > q >= 2, and for a positive real number alpha, what analogous questions and theory can be developed for the fractional parts of the products alpha times (p/q)^n for n = 0, 1, 2, ...?

evidence.quote: Naturally, one can consider analogous problems for the products alpha(p/q)^n (n = 0, 1, 2, ...) where alpha is again a positive number, and p and q are integers satisfying p > q >= 2, (p,q) = 1.
